firstRoundFindings: quiz.q1: Option 2's why incorrectly calls $3+1$ adding the coefficient to $x$. The coefficient is $2$; this distractor ignores the coefficient and computes $x+1$.
quiz.q2: Option 1's why says the negative signs were ignored, but $2\times1-1=1$ retains the negative constant. Specify that only the negative sign of the coefficient was ignored.
quiz.q6: Option 3's why implies that any lines with equal gradients never cross, overlooking coincident lines. Qualify the statement as distinct lines with equal gradients.

theory: The fact that a bigger coefficient of $x$ makes a line steeper is false for negative coefficients. Steepness depends on the magnitude of the coefficient, as stated in booklet lines 3968–3970; for example, $m=-3$ is steeper than $m=-1$.
summary: Corrected the distractor explanations in quiz.q1, quiz.q2 and quiz.q6 to identify the precise coefficient mistakes and qualify the equal-gradient statement for distinct lines. Corrected the theory fact to base steepness on the magnitude of the coefficient, including a negative-coefficient example; no whole items were removed and all other content was preserved.
reviewSummary: All three requested quiz questions have exactly one correct option, accurate working and distractor explanations, and supported booklet question types. The theory agrees with the booklet's graphing sequence and descriptions of direction and steepness, with no required repairs.
